overview: Success needs in-depth knowledge of modules 3 and 4 plus practical skills; many marks were lost through imprecise definitions and missing working.
State the equation, substitute and evaluate; in 'show' questions finish with the unrounded value then the rounded one.
Both Level of Response questions revealed shallow understanding of practical techniques and procedures.
Many did not know how to relate a straight-line equation to gradient and intercept or how to get uncertainties from a worst acceptable line.
Weaker candidates misused technical terms (e.g. mass vs weight, 'energy' vs 'kinetic energy') and omitted explanations of procedures.
assessment_for_learning: Practise ratio and proportionality questions, including finding the constant of proportionality.
Practise finding constants from gradient and y-intercept, and drawing worst acceptable lines through error bars to estimate uncertainty.
Calculation routine: write the equation, substitute, consider units, rearrange, evaluate, check the answer is sensible (see OCR Maths Skills Handbook).
Record and read data using the units in table column headings (e.g. THz).
Develop practical skills so you can describe methods (e.g. ray tracing) and suggest improvements.
Know and apply the two conditions for total internal reflection.
Draw stationary wave patterns in open and closed tubes and find the wavelength and frequency for each.
